name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis; BRIEF ratifies the /spec:mocks approved set) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each `--via loop`; /spec:design, /spec:build, and /spec:review remain each stage's direct entry, spec-build-driver.js and spec-review-driver.js stepped: admission, wave derivation, gate resolution, red-check, the final gate, scope-reconcile, legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros, and verdict derived by verdict.js, with test-author dispatch, per-wave worker dispatch, repair, reviewer dispatch, and dispositions held by the session) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.94.0 — questions on the wireframe (brief 22a): every inferred/invented product assumption the session writes while drawing a journey is pinned as a question (`ledger add … --screen <label>`, or `ledger ask --id <rowId> --screen <label>`) on the screen it belongs to; the served page answers it (`Yes, that's right` / `No, it's…` + text / `Later`), the answer writes the ledger row's status (`confirmed`/`overridden` + date, via new `POST /__notes/answer`) before resolving the note, and `journey-approved`/`variant-picked`/`approved` refuse while a question is unanswered, naming the ledger ids first; free-form notes gain an optional `reason` (missing-screen · wrong-direction · wrong-words · other) and the mock-page composer gains a scope toggle; `notes open` prints an open-questions block first and `ledger counts` gains a derived catch-provenance line (`question · note · unlinked`, from `addressed.ledgerRow`) — no new ledger column. 7.93.0 — mocks ends at wireframes (ADR-0008 amending ADR-0006, brief 22a): `/spec:mocks`'s chain drops `SKIN` and `REVIEW`, gains `SIGNOFF` (`SEED → SHAPES → WIREFRAMES → THEME → SIGNOFF → APPROVED`); `direction-composed` recomposes the seed's dense screen per direction (a second at most, never a full-product skin); `--mark approved` stamps every top-level mock `data-status="approved"` itself and records the sign-off stop's own decider — `--decider` is a retired flag; a host checkpointed mid-SKIN or mid-REVIEW derives THEME or SIGNOFF from its existing marks on the next run, nothing on disk is deleted, and ledger rows written under the retired step names keep parsing. 7.92.0 — post-close AC-pin drift becomes /spec:doctor check 17 (advisory): new `ac-drift.js` (`spec-paths ac-drift`) re-derives, for every `done` spec dated on or after the v7 cutover, the acceptance criteria no test-classified file cites and no sanction covers — `SHALL CONTINUE TO`, `[oracle:]`, `[pre-green:]`, or the new `[retired: <specs/… or docs/adr/… path>]` tag (an uncited `[retired:]` is itself the finding `retired-uncited`); `--json` for machines, `inapplicable — no specs/` is not a finding. `V7_APPLIES_FROM` lifts to lib/spec-sections.js (promise-sweep imports it) and `DEFAULT_TEST_GLOBS` is exported from lib/host-config.js. ci-gate-parity.js gains six behavioural regression pins. Four never-passed flags are deleted: render-gate `--no-boot`, promise-sweep `--applies-from`, registry-check `--timeout-ms`, design-atlas `stop open --question` (`question` is always null from the CLI); mocks-driver documents `ledger add` and its `--dependents` flag.
